content: Two viable mechanisms for nightly pg_dump-to-R2: (1) host systemd timer running a bash script that does 'docker exec <postgres-accessory> pg_dump ... | gzip' then uploads via aws-cli ('aws s3 cp ... --endpoint-url https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com') or rclone (S3-compatible provider=Cloudflare config) - simple, no external dependency, but R2 credentials must live in a host-side env file. (2) A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (on.schedule cron) that SSHes into the host (reusing the existing deploy SSH key) and runs the same dump+upload command, with R2 credentials injected transiently from GitHub repo secrets into the SSH session - never persisted on host disk. GitHub's public-repo 60-day scheduled-workflow auto-disable does NOT apply to private repos (confirmed via GitHub's own docs), so that specific risk is moot for a private solo-dev repo; GitHub's schedule trigger remains documented as best-effort/can lag under platform load, which is an acceptable tradeoff for a nightly (not time-critical) job. A purpose-built sidecar image (eeshugerman/postgres-backup-s3) exists and supports S3_ENDPOINT overrides for R2, but the repo is archived (June 2025, read-only) with no confirmed ARM64 image variant - not recommended given this project's ARM64-only host.
